title: mocoder backlog v1
description: Guided path to build a project by hand. User texts in the user's language, identifiers in the code in English. The guidance level (guided/hints/autonomous) is NOT here: it is a user setting.

summary.description: What the finished program will do, in 1-3 sentences.

level.description: The starting level of the user the path is meant for.

estimate_hours.description: Estimated hours to complete everything at the given level.

env.description: Optional: devcontainer.json or compose file for a reproducible environment.

conventions.description: Project rules valid for the whole path (structure, naming, security, git, database…), in the form 'Area — rule'. The student always sees them and the Reviewer checks them.

tasks.description: In execution order. A task can depend only on tasks that precede it.

path.description: Path relative to the project root, with '/'. No '..', no absolute paths.

goal.description: What works at the end of the milestone.

learn.description: Concepts taught: keys to look up the theory in the vault.

theory.description: Markdown. First the why, then the how, then the typical mistakes.

search.description: Web searches to go deeper into the task's topic even without AI: short, specific phrases with language and concept, preferably in English (e.g. 'java record compact constructor validation'). No links: they might not exist.

hints.description: From the concept to the solution: the last one is the complete solution.

checks.description: Executed in order from the project root. The task is done when they all pass.

review.description: What the Reviewer looks at, as in a real code review.

file.description: given=true: provided file (test, configuration), written by the app and not to be modified. Otherwise: a file the user works on; content is the initial skeleton, used only if the file does not exist yet.

solution.description: Separate file (.mocoder/solution.yaml), hidden from the user: for every task, the complete content of the files the user writes in that task, once the task is done. It is used to verify that the checks fail before the work and pass after.

run.description: A single command, without && or pipes, that works on Windows, macOS and Linux. Stdin closed. The check passes only if the command ends with exit code 0 (and, if expect is present, the output contains it): a task cannot have a failing test as its goal.

expect.description: Optional: regex that must appear in the output.
